lawyer: For the petitioner : Mr. Minhazuddin, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Nawab Ali, Advocate-On-Record. For respondent No. 1 : Mr. Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-On-Record. For Respondent No. 2 : Not represented.
parties:
Md. Baziur Rahman Sikder ------ Accused-Petitioner.
Versus Mrs. Tahera Begum Alias Shamima and another ------- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J : The accused Petitioner has filed this petition for leave to appeal challenging the judgment and order dated 7-12-95 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Misc. Case No. 864 of 1994, discharging the Rule and thereby refusing to transfer C. R. Case No. 374C of 1994 under section 6(5) of the Muslim Family Law Ordinance pending in the Court of Magistrate. 1st Class `Ka` Region, Bogra to any Court of Magistrate at Dhaka. 

 3. The accused-petitioner filed an application for transfer of the case from the Court of Mr. Md. Shamsul Alam, Magistrate, 1st Class, Bogra to any Court' of Magistrate, 1st Class, Dhaka under section 526 of the code of Criminal Procedure on the ground that the cause of action of this case arose at Dhaka, all the witnesses of the case reside at Dhaka and as such the learned Magistrate at Bogra has no jurisdiction to try the case and that the case was filed at Bogra only to harass and humiliate the petitioner who was at one time an S. D. 0. of Bogra. 

 4. It appears that the learned Judges on Consideration of the materials on record found that respondent No. 1 resides at Bogra in the house of her father and that most of the witnesses are residents of Bogra. The learned Judges of the High Court Division also found that the petitioner failed to make out a case of transfer from Bogra to Dhaka and consequently refused to transfer the case. A. transfer under section 526 of the code is a discretionary matter and the learned Judges having exercised that discretion judicially the same calls for no interference.
